selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main truth is introduced at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The passage introduces the reality that beings in the universe help one another in ways far beyond their own power.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this co-operation cannot be explained by the beings themselves?
questions.answer: Because the help and coordination go beyond their own ability, awareness, and strength.

questions.question: How do the clouds function in this chain of help?
questions.answer: They are described as aiding plant life.

questions.question: How does the animal world support human beings?
questions.answer: Animals are shown as serving human life and benefit.

questions.question: Why is the example of an infant’s nourishment important in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that a helpless being receives what it needs without having the ability to secure it by itself.

questions.question: What bodily example is used to show inward co-operation?
questions.answer: Food particles are directed to the body’s cells to renew and support them.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the universe to a palace?
questions.answer: To show that it is managed in an organized, purposeful, and well-run way.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the co-operation of inanimate things?
questions.answer: They must be directed by the power and command of a compassionate, wise, and glorious Sustainer.

questions.question: What range of things is used to show the vastness of balance and preservation?
questions.answer: The passage moves from heavenly bodies down to organs, limbs, and even tiny particles in living bodies.

questions.question: What does assigning duties to created things imply about the universe?
questions.answer: It implies that creation operates under purpose, direction, and responsibility rather than chance.

questions.question: According to the passage, what shared reality appears among created things?
questions.answer: A widespread pattern of mutual assistance appears among them.

questions.question: What does the phrase about constant upheaval suggest about the world?
questions.answer: It suggests that the world is always in motion and change, not stable or self-sufficient.

questions.question: What does the image of milk for a baby communicate about divine care?
questions.answer: It shows gentle and immediate mercy for the weakest and most needy.

questions.question: How does the nourishment of body cells strengthen the main claim?
questions.answer: It shows that even inside the body there is a directed and purposeful system of support.

questions.question: What larger attribute is shown by these many examples of support and provision?
questions.answer: They show a caring lordship that manages the whole universe.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress that solid and lifeless things are neither aware nor feeling?
questions.answer: To show that their orderly service cannot come from themselves.

questions.question: How does the passage use very large and very small examples together?
questions.answer: It uses both to show that the same wise rule appears throughout all levels of existence.

questions.question: Why are fruits like corn and pomegranates mentioned with cosmic structures?
questions.answer: To show that careful order exists in ordinary earthly things just as it does in massive heavenly systems.

questions.question: In the passage’s argument, what is the role of this whole section on co-operation?
questions.answer: It provides one major part of the universe’s witness to the existence and qualities of its Sustainer.

questions.question: How does the passage end this discussion?
questions.answer: It says only a brief indication has been given because this testimony has been explained elsewhere.

questions.question: What central idea ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: The whole passage centers on the universe-wide harmony of things helping one another under divine rule.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the claim that co-operation goes beyond the capacity of creatures?
questions.answer: It can be inferred that another power is organizing and directing them.

questions.question: How do clouds fit into the larger system described?
questions.answer: They play a supporting role for plant life within the wider chain of benefit.

questions.question: What role do animals have in this sequence?
questions.answer: They are shown as a means of support and service for human beings.
